__doc:
Issue #1826 — the POSITIVE corpus for step 3 (contextNeed + deterministic retrieval).

cases-1826.json is 100% negative: every correct answer is 0. It proved the claim
checker (step 2), which can only DROP a finding. It cannot prove step 3, because
no case in it declares a contextNeed at all — needOf() falls through to diff-only,
so retrieveForShard never runs there.

Here the correct answer is 1 for the paired A/B cases: a rule the customer wrote
that CANNOT fire without repository context. Each is run twice — once with the
need declared, once without (the -CONTROL twin, byte-identical otherwise). The
gap between the two IS the value of step 3; if there is no gap, the feature does
nothing.

C is the guard in the other direction: retrieval must not manufacture a finding
where the sibling really exists.

NOTE: these cases carry a raw `patch` as well as `patchWithLinesStr`, the way
production FileChange objects do. `diffOf` in rule-context.retriever.ts prefers
`patch`, and symbol extraction cannot parse the line-numbered format — a case
with only patchWithLinesStr reports symbol-references as UNMET.

cases.why: The PR adds a new route handler and NO companion test exists — not in the PR, not in the repository. The rule is supposed to fire. Only a sibling-path existence check can establish that; the hunk shows the controller alone.

rule.title: Every new HTTP route handler ships with a test
rule.rule: A new HTTP route handler must be accompanied by a test file next to it (`<name>.spec.ts`). Untested endpoints are the most common source of regressions.

cases.why: src/shared/strings.ts ALREADY exports `slugify`. The PR adds a second copy in src/blog/slug.ts, which is exactly what the rule forbids. Nothing in the hunk says so: only a repository grep does. The claim checker cannot help here — it can drop a finding, never create one.
cases.prBody: Adds slug generation for blog posts.

rule.title: Do not reimplement a helper that already exists
rule.rule: Before adding a small utility function, use the one already published in `src/shared`. Duplicated helpers drift apart and the two behaviours diverge silently.
